forces.title: Rising UHNWI Population Fuels Demand for Wealth Management
forces.description: India’s Ultra-High-Net-Worth Individual (UHNWI) population is projected to significantly increase from 19,877 in 2026 to 25,217 by 2031, supported by deepening capital markets and digitalization. This demographic growth creates substantial demand for sophisticated wealth management, advisory, and alternative investment services. Financial institutions, including asset managers and wealth managers, can capture this expanding market by offering tailored solutions in inheritance planning, business continuity, global mobility, and specialized investment products, significantly boosting AUM and fee-based income across the Capital Markets sector.

forces.title: Increasing Retail Participation and Digital Connectivity in Capital Markets
forces.description: The Indian equity market is experiencing a surge in retail participation, with one-fifth of households connected to stock markets and over 18 crore demat accounts. Digital platforms and financial inclusion initiatives have facilitated a record 2.32 crore new investors in 2024. This expanding investor base, coupled with increasing household allocation to equities and mutual funds via SIPs, is a strong tailwind for brokerages, asset management companies, and investment banks, driving growth in equity market turnover, AUM, and demand for diversified financial products. It underscores the potential for sustained market expansion.

forces.title: AI and Agentic AI Reshaping Capital Markets Operations
forces.description: AI is fundamentally transforming capital markets by enabling more autonomous decision-making across credit, liquidity, compliance, and trade execution. The shift from AI-assisted to AI-initiated processes, including AI-powered agents for customer engagement and risk management, signifies a structural change. For brokerages, asset managers, and market infrastructure, this means enhanced efficiency, faster transaction processing, and improved risk outcomes. The adoption of AI-native operating models and investment in AI-ready data will be crucial for firms to remain competitive, leading to re-imagined workflows and significant operational leverage in Capital Markets.

forces.title: Tokenised Financial Assets Transform Capital Markets with Enhanced Liquidity
forces.description: Tokenised financial assets are ushering in a new era for capital markets, promising greater efficiency, accessibility, and liquidity. This structural shift involves programmable transactions, near real-time settlement, and improved interoperability across digital rails. For exchanges, debt markets, and investment banks, tokenization creates opportunities to modernize infrastructure, facilitate atomic settlement of securities, and offer new forms of digital assets. Institutions are increasingly competing on programmable liquidity services and 24x7 market infrastructure, signifying a fundamental redefinition of asset classes and transaction mechanisms within the Capital Markets sector.

forces.title: Fintech IPO Activity Plunges Amid Market Uncertainty and AI Impact
forces.description: Global fintech IPO activity experienced a dramatic fall in H1 2026, with VC exit value for public listings dropping from $64.9 billion in 2025 to $5.3 billion. Similarly, PE exit value declined from $16.8 billion to $2.0 billion. This severe slowdown is a key risk for Investment Banking & Brokerage and Private Equity & Venture Capital nodes, impacting deal volumes and potential returns. Factors include public fintech equity values falling below listing prices, investor reassessment of software businesses due to AI's influence, and broader market liquidity uncertainty, posing challenges for fund exits and new listings.

forces.title: India's Sovereign AI Ecosystem Strengthens Financial Sector Capabilities
forces.description: India's strategic investments in building a sovereign AI ecosystem, encompassing infrastructure, talent, and innovation, act as a significant tailwind for Capital Markets. Strengthening domestic AI capabilities enhances competitiveness and resilience across financial services. For Capital Markets firms, this provides access to advanced tools for risk assessment, algorithmic trading, customer engagement, and data analysis. The availability of robust, nationally controlled AI resources fosters trust and accelerates the adoption of AI-native operating models, ensuring data sovereignty and contributing to India's leadership in future-ready financial systems, enhancing market efficiency and security.

forces.title: Open Finance and Consent-Portable Data Revolutionize Wealth Advisory
forces.description: Open finance and consent-based data ecosystems, particularly through Account Aggregator (AA) and Unified Lending Interface (ULI) frameworks, are driving a structural change in Capital Markets. These platforms enable customers and MSMEs to share verified financial histories, accelerating data-driven services. For Asset Management & Wealth, this means personalized wealth and investment advisory becomes more efficient and accurate, as lenders combine diverse data sources to construct sector-specific credit products and provide contextual advice. This enhances financial inclusion and fosters innovation by leveraging comprehensive, consented data, improving customer-centricity and service delivery.

forces.title: Consolidation Intensifies in Wealth and Asset Management Sector
forces.description: A significant structural change is underway in the wealth and asset management space, driven by private equity investors actively seeking consolidation and roll-up opportunities. This trend suggests a strategic move towards building scale and leveraging synergies within the industry, leading to increased M&A activity. For existing asset management companies and wealth managers, this could mean heightened competitive pressure, but also opportunities for strategic partnerships or acquisitions to expand market share and improve operational efficiency. The intensifying consolidation will reshape the competitive landscape, potentially leading to fewer, larger players dominating the market.

forces.title: Escalating Cyber and Quantum Threats to Financial Infrastructure
forces.description: The financial sector faces escalating cybersecurity risks, amplified by Generative AI enabling sophisticated phishing and vulnerability exploitation. A critical emerging threat is the need for quantum readiness, with firms re-examining long-term security of systems against future cryptographic risks. For Capital Markets, this poses a high risk to market infrastructure, data providers, and transaction security. Investment in quantum-resistant authentication frameworks, robust governance, and continuous real-time threat intelligence are imperative to safeguard digital identities, payments, and financial infrastructure against increasingly complex, AI-driven threat vectors and potential quantum disruption.

forces.title: Strong Policy Support Boosts Financial Services Digitalization and Inclusion
forces.description: Government and RBI policies provide strong tailwinds for Capital Markets through banking reforms, digital initiatives, and financial inclusion schemes. Measures like UPI-based credit, AI-driven payments, and expanded financial literacy programs improve access and efficiency across the financial ecosystem. Regulatory innovation, institutional initiatives, and support for interoperable digital infrastructure (DPI) foster a secure and technology-enabled environment. This policy backing encourages innovation, increases formalization, and broadens access to financial services, positively impacting areas like asset management, brokerage, and market infrastructure by expanding the addressable market and streamlining operations.

forces.title: Increased Investment in Core Technology and Digital Asset Infrastructure
forces.description: Infrastructure is becoming a major investment priority across financial services, including for Capital Markets. This structural change is driven by the growing focus on stablecoins and digital assets, necessitating robust infrastructure for their scaling and interoperability. Additionally, traditional financial institutions are upgrading their core infrastructure to enhance competitiveness and protect data, leading to significant capital deployment in technology. This trend supports market infrastructure entities and technology providers, ensuring the underlying rails for capital markets remain resilient, scalable, and secure amidst evolving digital asset landscapes and increasing transactional complexity, driving innovation across the sector.

viewpoints.title: AI Adoption Propels Banking and Capital Markets to Transformation Forefront
viewpoints.description: KPMG projects that banking and capital markets will be at the forefront of AI expansion over the next year, indicating a strong positive outlook for technological integration. The financial sector is entering a critical phase of AI transformation, moving from pilot phases to enterprise-wide production environments. This shift is expected to reshape business operations and customer experiences fundamentally, with confidence in AI's future remaining high despite initial adoption challenges. Such advancements will drive efficiency, enhance decision-making, and create new competitive advantages across capital markets firms.

viewpoints.title: Tokenised Financial Assets Reshaping Next-Generation Capital Markets for Efficiency
viewpoints.description: KPMG highlights that tokenised financial assets are fundamentally reshaping next-generation capital markets by enabling greater efficiency, accessibility, and liquidity. This transformation is driven by programmable ownership, real-time settlement capabilities, and improved interoperability, creating significant opportunities to enhance market access and operational efficiency. The evolving landscape of digital asset markets, supported by financial institutions implementing blockchain-enabled solutions and digital asset infrastructure, positions capital markets for a period of accelerated innovation and growth, driven by these new forms of digital value exchange.

viewpoints.title: Indian Savers Increasingly Active in Equities and Mutual Funds Post-COVID
viewpoints.description: McKinsey notes that post-COVID-19 Indian savers are becoming more financially active, increasingly directing incremental savings toward market-linked instruments like equities and mutual funds through Systematic Investment Plans (SIPs). This trend indicates a growing appetite for formal financial market participation beyond traditional bank deposits, supporting the asset management and brokerage segments of Capital Markets. While insurance adoption has not kept pace, the structural reallocation of household portfolios towards capital market products suggests sustained investor confidence and a positive demand outlook for investment products and services, driving folio growth and AUM.

viewpoints.title: Indian Capital Markets Exhibit Strong Investor Confidence with Record IPOs
viewpoints.description: IBEF reports that India's capital markets are demonstrating robust investor confidence, evidenced by record IPO mobilization and significant growth in market capitalization. The substantial pipeline of upcoming IPOs for 2026, alongside a surge in new investors connecting to stock markets, reflects expanding direct equity market engagement and substantial wealth creation. This sustained growth trajectory, supported by rising retail participation and deeper capital markets, underpins a positive outlook for investment banking, brokerage, and asset management activities, indicating a thriving ecosystem for capital formation and wealth accumulation.

viewpoints.title: Wealth and Asset Management Space Ripe for Consolidation and Growth
viewpoints.description: KPMG indicates a positive outlook for the wealth and asset management space, anticipating increased activity and consolidation. Private Equity investors, in particular, are actively exploring roll-up opportunities, suggesting a strategic focus on leveraging synergies and building scale within the sector. This trend reflects growing investor interest in established, proven business models capable of delivering value. The drive for consolidation is likely to reshape the competitive landscape, fostering efficiency and potentially leading to more sophisticated product offerings and enhanced financial performance, especially as firms seek to expand offerings and gain scale.

viewpoints.title: Fintech IPO Activity Declines Dramatically Amid Market Uncertainty and AI Impact
viewpoints.description: KPMG reports a significant decline in global fintech IPO activity in H1 2026 following a strong 2025, with VC exit value plummeting from $64.9 billion in 2025 to $5.3 billion in H1 2026, and PE exit value falling from $16.8 billion to $2.0 billion. This slowdown is attributed to public fintech equity values falling below listing prices, investor reassessment of software businesses due to AI's impact, and general market liquidity uncertainty. The reduced IPO market suggests a cautious environment for investment banking and private equity firms seeking exit routes, indicating potential headwinds for deal volumes.

These factors are expected to shape the mutual fund industry, suggesting evolving product preferences and a supportive regulatory environment.
